title: Atom cost + latency lens — explorations and sketchbook
content:
Context and goal:

This note collects exploratory UX directions for a token-level cost+latency "lens" inside Console. We intentionally call the unit an "atom" in early designs to signal the UI is about the smallest billing/rendering unit (token/byte/step) and to avoid overloading the existing "token" vocabulary across reports. The goal: give engineers and platform owners an ultra-fast way to diagnose cost anomalies and tail latency at the atomic level, then pivot to meaningful rollups (invocation, route, model variant).

Primary user personas:
- Platform engineer (SRE/Infra) who needs to find regressions in latency percentiles after a rollout.
- Product engineer responsible for unit economics per feature route.
- Solutions engineer debugging customer reports of large monthly bills.

Design principles:
- Fast signal-to-insight: show anomaly indicators at-a-glance, allow one-click pivot to the invocation list or traces.
- Multi-scale: sparkline for per-atom time series, ridgeline for distribution, and aggregate cards for quick KPI checks.
- Non-destructive exploration: interactions are filters, not destructive edits.
- Context-first: show invocation context (prompt length, model variant, quantization profile) when drilling down.

Key metrics surfaced (atom lens):
- atom_cost_usd: cost contributed by a single atomic unit, normalized and shown as micro-units (e.g., $0.00000x).
- atom_latency_ms: observed latency for that atom (if measurable); aggregated into p50/p95/p99.
- atom_position: position in invocation (prefix, generation, assistant message) to correlate cost spikes with position.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: proportion of atoms served from cache in the selected slice.
- model_variant: model id + quantization tag; used to color / facet charts.

Wireframe explorations (three variants) — high level descriptions:

Variant A — Sparkline Rows (compact, dense)
- Left column: microcards (selected time window, total atoms, avg atom cost, avg atom latency).
- Middle: vertical list of top 8 affected routes. Each row shows a tiny sparkline (30–90s window) of atom_cost_usd with a heat ribbon behind showing latency bins (fast/ok/slow).
- Right: preview pane that shows the currently hovered atom group: small excerpt of prompt, invocation id, model variant, and button to open full trace.
- Interaction notes: click on a row converts the sparkline to a small waterfall of atom costs for a single invocation; shift-click selects multiple routes to compare.

Variant B — Ridgeline + Heat Ribbon (emphasis on distribution)
- Top: global ridgeline density of atom_latency_ms across chosen period, each ridge stacked by model_variant.
- Middle: cost heat ribbon timeline (multi-colored band where intensity = total cost per bucket, color = median latency bucket). Hover shows percent of atoms in each latency band.
- Bottom: compact table with sample invocations (id, route, atom count, top atom contributors).
- Interaction notes: brushing on ridgeline filters the timeline; clicking a model in legend isolates it. Good for investigating distribution changes after a deploy.

Variant C — Contextual Rewind (investigation-first)
- Left: timeline with selectable time cursor and contextual breadcrumbs (deploys, config changes, quant profiles).
- Center: atom playback where as you scrub the cursor you see the sequence of atom_cost_usd and latency for a single selected invocation; each atom is tappable to reveal prompt excerpt and cost breakdown.
- Right: suggested remediation actions (auto-scaling recommendation, quantization suggestion, cache warm policy) and quick links to create a rollback or create an incident.
- Interaction notes: aimed at incident response flow.

Prototype micro-interactions and affordances:
- Sparklines have an overlaid band for p99 latency; red ticks indicate dropped/errored atoms.
- Hover microtooltip shows: avg atom cost, latency percentile, proportion of total invocation cost, sample token text (first 64 chars), and a one-click copy-to-clipboard for invocation id.
- Color encoding: cool -> warm for latency buckets; separate hue for model variants to avoid conflation with latency colors.
- Lightweight animation when switching time windows to preserve user's mental map.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI surfaces per-atom cost + p95 latency for a selected route over a 30m/6h/24h window.
- Sparkline rows are paginated and can be filtered by model_variant and deploy tag.
- Drilldown: from a sparkline row to an invocation detail page with the atom sequence, sample prompt, and latency breakdown.
- Export: ability to export the current view as CSV with atom-level rows (invocation_id, atom_index, atom_cost_usd, atom_latency_ms, model_variant).

Open questions / risks:
- Storage/ingest cost: atom-level retention at high qps is expensive. We need a backend policy: retain full atom sequence for 7d by default and sampled sequences beyond that. Need cost estimate from infra team. (Linked: PROD-4123)
- Privacy: sample token text is sensitive. Masking policy required for PII; default to first 32 chars with redaction and a tenant-level toggle for raw preview.
- Attribution: how do we attribute shared tokens between system prompts and user turns? Need canonicalization rules in ingestion.
- Performance: rendering thousands of sparklines could be heavy on client — client-side virtualization required.

Backlog grooming list (candidate tickets / epics) — prioritized:
- ATOM-01: storage policy proposal and costing estimate (owner: Jorge) — depend on infra.
- ATOM-02: minimal API: atom aggregates per-route (30m/6h/24h) + sample invocation endpoint (owner: Evan).
- ATOM-03: client component: sparkline-row + heat ribbon (owner: Maya) — include virtualization.
- ATOM-04: hover microtooltip content design + privacy toggles (owner: Aisha) — legal review.
- ATOM-05: ridgeline distribution component + legend interactions (owner: designer TBD).
- ATOM-06: export CSV feature + quotas (owner: product-ops).

Low-fidelity sketches (text descriptions you can hand to a designer):
- Sketch 1: Tall left rail of microcards, then a two-column grid: left column vertical list of rows (compact text + sparkline), right column large preview. Include microfilters above rows (model, route, deploy).
- Sketch 2: Full-bleed ridgeline across top third, heat ribbon across middle, table across bottom. On hover, show vertical guideline and highlight matching row in table.
- Sketch 3: Timeline scrubber with playback control; atoms appear as small circles on the scrub timeline; clicking circle shows atom details in a bottom drawer.

Suggested microcopy and labels:
- Lens toggle label: "Atom lens (per‑unit econ + latency)"
- Sparkline tooltip header: "Atoms: cost + latency snapshot"
- Preview CTA: "Open invocation trace"

Next steps and owners:
- Short-term (1–2 sprints): build ATOM-02 API contract, start client skeleton for sparkline rows (ATOM-03), and legal review on token preview policy (ATOM-04). Owners: Evan, Maya, Aisha.
- Medium (3–6 sprints): backend retention policy and sampling (ATOM-01), ridgeline component and export feature (ATOM-05/06).
- Research spike: estimate CPU/GPU cost to compute atom-level latency percentiles from traces vs. ingest-time aggregation. (Owner: infra analytics)

Notes and meeting history:
- Ran quick design crit 2026-03-01 with eng, s-re, and product; need follow-up with infra to validate storage numbers.
- Customer signals: two enterprise customers reported unexplained 2–3x month-over-month increases where cost concentrated in a small set of very long prompts. Atom lens would help identify that surface.

Appendix: example sample flow (short):
1) Product engineer opens Console -> selects route -> toggles "Atom lens" -> sees sparkline rows.
2) She notices route X has recurring red spikes on p99 band.
3) Clicks the top row -> preview shows sample invocation with 180 atoms where atoms 72–90 contribute 65% of cost.
4) She opens invocation trace -> sees model variant changed at step 70 due to conditional routing and k/v cache miss.
5) Creates a ticket (PROD-4123) to add a cache-warm step to the canary rollout.

If useful I can create a quick Figma board with annotated wires for Variant A/B/C and export assets for dev.
